int_name: N BROAD ST & W THOMPSON ST

result.summary: The intersection features a marked zebra crosswalk and a substantial concrete refuge island, which significantly improves pedestrian safety on this wide multi-lane roadway. While sidewalks are in good condition and traffic signals are present, the overall scale of the street remains car-oriented with multiple travel lanes.

hazards.name: Wide roadway exposure
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic, increasing the risk of multi-threat crashes despite the presence of a median.

hazards.name: Lack of visible pedestrian signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are clearly visible, which may lead to confusion about crossing phases.
hazards.location_in_image: Traffic signal poles at the intersection

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install high-visibility pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear crossing information.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve sight lines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle green light.

result.summary: The intersection is equipped with high-visibility zebra crosswalks, curb ramps, and dedicated pedestrian signals. While basic infrastructure is present, the environment lacks physical buffers like street trees or bollards to separate pedestrians from vehicle traffic. The wide, open design of the intersection may encourage higher vehicle speeds during turns.

hazards.name: Lack of physical buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation such as trees, bollards, or planters between the sidewalk and the moving traffic lanes.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the sidewalk edges on both sides of the street.

hazards.name: Wide turning radius
hazards.description: The corner geometry allows for relatively fast vehicle turns, increasing risk to pedestrians in the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: The corner of the brick building on the left side of the intersection.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distance and slow turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planters
interventions.description: Install street trees or large planters to provide a vertical buffer between pedestrians and traffic.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles get a green light.

result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility continental crosswalks and wide sidewalks, providing a basic level of pedestrian infrastructure. However, the multi-lane roadway creates a significant crossing distance without a refuge island, and parked vehicles near the intersection may limit visibility.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a refuge island, increasing exposure time to vehicles.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles on the right side of the street are positioned close to the crosswalk, potentially obscuring pedestrians from oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway along the curb

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a raised island in the center of the roadway to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The intersection features marked zebra crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and sidewalks, providing a basic level of pedestrian infrastructure. Safety is compromised by wide crossing distances and parked vehicles that obstruct sightlines between drivers and pedestrians. The lack of physical traffic calming measures like curb extensions increases the risk of high-speed vehicle turns.

hazards.name: Parked vehicles near crossing
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection corners obstruct the visibility between pedestrians waiting to cross and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs of the intersecting street on the right and left sides.

hazards.name: Wide turning radii
hazards.description: The intersection geometry allows for wide turning paths, which can encourage vehicles to maintain higher speeds when turning across pedestrian paths.
hazards.location_in_image: At the corners of the intersection.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and improve visibility by moving pedestrians further into the street before they cross.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalks to ensure clear sightlines for both pedestrians and drivers.
